financials_interim.notes: Renuka City Hotels PLC (RENU), a small city hotel operator majority-owned (71.88%) by Renuka Hotels PLC, Colombo. SINGLE-ENTITY basis (no subsidiaries/associates disclosed anywhere in this filing -- no 'Group' column, no consolidation note, no NCI -- stored as one GROUP row per this database's single-entity convention). Q1 FY2026/27 ('Quarter Ended 30-Jun-26') vs Q1 FY2025/26 (30-Jun-25) comparative, both on the face Statement of Profit or Loss and Other Comprehensive Income (page 1); a third column (31-Mar-26, the full prior FY) also appears on the face statements but is NOT a QoQ-comparable quarter and is not used here. CRITICAL STRUCTURAL POINT (not generic commentary -- quantified below): RENU's PBT growth this quarter is overwhelmingly a FINANCIAL-INVESTMENT-PORTFOLIO story, not a hotel-operations story, though the hotel business itself also grew genuinely. Profit From Operations (the hotel business: rooms, F&B, other operating income) was Rs.74,943k (2026) vs Rs.43,564k (2025), +72.0% YoY -- a real, quantified operating improvement. But Net Finance Income (a single combined line on the face P&L, not split into finance income vs finance cost) was Rs.795,733k (2026) vs Rs.245,226k (2025), +224.5% YoY -- and this single line contributed Rs.550,507k of the Group's total Rs.581,886k PBT increase (870,676 vs 288,790 PY), i.e. ~94.6% of the ENTIRE PBT improvement came from Net Finance Income, with the hotel operating-profit increase (+Rs.31,379k) contributing only ~5.4%. The Net Finance Income line is not decomposed on the face statements, but the Cash Flow Statement's add-back reconciliation (page 1) shows only Rs.158,969k Interest Income + Rs.33,987k Dividend Income + Rs.18,464k Profit on disposals of shares = Rs.211,420k of conventional finance income this quarter -- leaving a Rs.584,313k residual (795,733 - 211,420) that is NOT itemised anywhere in this filing, almost certainly unrealised fair-value gains on the Rs.7,431,559k 'Investments in financial asset' current-asset line (a large FVTPL-type portfolio, distinct from the separate Rs.1,188,136k Fair Value Reserve of FVOCI equity investments sitting in equity) -- a genuine, material disclosure gap flagged here and in gaps_note, since it is the single largest driver of this quarter's headline profit growth. Total 'Investments in financial asset(s)' across both non-current (Rs.2,243,034k) and current (Rs.7,431,559k) sum to Rs.9,674,593k, i.e. 72.0% of Total Assets (Rs.13,439,013k) -- more than 28x the Rs.333,674k carrying value of Property, Plant & Equipment (the actual hotel building/assets) -- confirming RENU is, by balance sheet composition, primarily an investment-holding entity that also operates a small city hotel, not primarily a hotel operator. REVENUE/OPERATING DRIVERS (hotel business, genuine YoY comparators disclosed on the face P&L): Revenue +45.0% YoY to Rs.63,551k (2025: Rs.43,823k); Cost of Sales +29.0% to Rs.(11,990)k (2025: Rs.(9,290)k); Gross Profit +49.3% to Rs.51,561k (2025: Rs.34,533k); Other Operating Income +65.7% to Rs.59,951k (2025: Rs.36,169k) -- this Other Operating Income line is now LARGER than core hotel Gross Profit, and is not itemised by source (rent, service charges, etc. are plausible for a hotel but not confirmed by the filing -- a genuine gap). Of the three opex lines, Marketing Expenses grew fastest, +146.1% YoY to Rs.4,804k (2025: Rs.1,952k) -- the single fastest-growing cost line, worth flagging specifically; Administrative Expenses grew +42.2% to Rs.20,694k (2025: Rs.14,557k); Salaries & Related Expenses grew only +4.1% to Rs.11,071k (2025: Rs.10,630k), the most contained cost line. Income Tax Expense actually FELL to Rs.2,000k from Rs.4,000k PY (-50%) despite the much larger pretax profit -- consistent with RENU's income being predominantly investment income (dividends, and likely BOI/exempt or concessionary-rate gains) rather than fully-taxable trading profit; the filing gives no further breakdown of the effective tax computation, a genuine gap. OTHER COMPREHENSIVE INCOME: Equity Investments at FVTOCI - Net Change in Fair Value SWUNG NEGATIVE this quarter, Rs.(45,331)k vs a Rs.166,042k GAIN in 2025 (-127.3% YoY, a Rs.211,373k unfavourable swing) -- this pulled Total Comprehensive Income growth down to +82.6% YoY (Rs.823,344k vs Rs.450,832k PY) despite Profit for the period growing a faster 205.1% -- i.e. the FVOCI portfolio (a SEPARATE investment book from the FVTPL-type portfolio driving Net Finance Income above) moved unfavourably even as the P&L-recognised investment income surged, a genuine and quantified divergence between the two investment books. BALANCE SHEET: Total Liabilities = Non-Current (73,098) + Current (54,615) = 127,713k; Total Equity (13,311,301) + Total Liabilities (127,713) = 13,439,014k, ties printed Total Assets 13,439,013k to within Rs.1k rounding. short_term_borrowings = Bank Overdraft (2,344k) only, the sole interest-bearing item disclosed; no long-term interest-bearing borrowings are disclosed anywhere in this filing (long_term_borrowings stored as 0) -- RENU appears effectively debt-free on conventional borrowings, consistent with its large investment-portfolio balance sheet. trade_payables = 'Trade & Other Payables' (30,551k) as printed, a combined line; trade_receivables is mapped to 'Other Receivables' (4,906k) as the closest analogous line -- the filing does NOT use a 'Trade Receivables' caption at all, a genuine presentational gap for a hotel business (which would typically have guest/agent receivables), flagged here. cash_and_equivalents=3,409,988k is the face BS 'Cash & Cash Equivalents'; the Cash Flow Statement's 'Cash and Cash Equivalents at the End of the Period' of Rs.3,407,643k is Rs.2,345k lower because it nets the Rs.2,344k Bank Overdraft against cash (3,409,988-2,344=3,407,644, ties to within Re.1 rounding) -- an EXPLICITLY RECONCILABLE definitional difference, not an unresolved gap. shares_in_issue = 7,000,000 (Note 5: 'Stated Capital is represented by 7.0 million Issued Shares'). EPS cross-check: 868,676 (Rs'000) / 7,000 (thousand shares) = Rs.124.097/share, ties disclosed Rs.124.10 exactly. depreciation_amortization=6,630 (Depreciation on Property, Plant & Equipment per the Cash Flow Statement; Intangible Assets are nil on the balance sheet at all three presented dates, so no amortisation applies). capex=0 this quarter (no PPE purchases disclosed for the current quarter, vs Rs.187k in the prior-year quarter); Rs.7,500k of PPE disposal proceeds were received this quarter (2025: nil), captured within cash_from_investing but not capex. NO SEGMENTAL NOTE, NO OCCUPANCY RATE OR AVERAGE ROOM RATE DISCLOSURE, and NO tourism-season qualitative commentary appear anywhere in this filing -- genuine, material disclosure gaps for a hotel operator, explicitly checked for and confirmed absent, flagged in gaps_note (unlike some CSE hotel-sector peers that do disclose occupancy/ADR).

thesis.thesis_text: Renuka City Hotels is, by balance-sheet composition, primarily an investment-holding entity that also operates a small city hotel: total financial-asset investments of Rs.9,674.59mn represent 72.0% of Total Assets (Rs.13,439.01mn) and over 28x the Rs.333.67mn PPE carrying value of the actual hotel. Q1 FY2026/27 PAT surged 205.1% YoY to Rs.868.68mn, but roughly 94.6% of the Rs.581.89mn PBT increase came from Net Finance Income (+224.5% YoY to Rs.795.73mn), of which only Rs.211.42mn is itemised (interest, dividends, disposal gains) -- leaving a Rs.584.31mn residual, almost certainly unrealised fair-value gains on the investment portfolio, that is not explained anywhere in the filing. The hotel business itself did grow genuinely (revenue +45.0% YoY, operating profit +72.0% to Rs.74.94mn), but contributed only ~5.4% of the total profit increase. A separate, OCI-recognised FVOCI equity portfolio moved the opposite direction this quarter (Rs.(45.33)mn vs. a Rs.166.04mn gain a year earlier), capping Total Comprehensive Income growth to 82.6% versus the 205.1% P&L profit growth -- a reminder that RENU's two investment books can diverge. The stock trades at a substantial ~0.42x discount to book value (NAV/share ~Rs.1,902 vs. price Rs.800) and a statistically very cheap ~1.6x annualized P/E, though the P/E is distorted by unrealised investment gains embedded in the earnings line and is not a clean operating multiple (interim filed 25-Aug-2026, source_doc_id 52449).
thesis.gaps_note: Macro & Industry Outlook (10% weight) unavailable -- renormalized across the remaining five pillars. Confidence is capped by having only one quarter of financials on file with no QoQ comparator. The single largest driver of this quarter's headline profit growth -- a Rs.584,313k residual within Net Finance Income, not itemised or explained in the filing -- is a genuine, material, unresolved uncertainty, not a confirmed operating gain, and this caps confidence materially. The filing also discloses no occupancy rate, ADR, or segmental note for the hotel business, and does not split Net Finance Income into finance income vs. finance cost, so finance_costs is stored as 0 by convention rather than as a confirmed zero.

financial_quality.rationale: Effectively debt-free (Rs.2,344k overdraft only) with a massive equity base (Rs.13,311.30mn) relative to total assets (Rs.13,439.01mn), but 94.6% of this quarter's PBT growth came from Net Finance Income, of which a Rs.584,313k residual (73% of that line) is entirely unitemised in the filing -- a material, unresolved profit-quality gap that caps the score despite the strong balance sheet.

growth_outlook.rationale: The underlying hotel business grew genuinely -- Revenue +45.0% YoY, hotel operating profit +72.0% YoY to Rs.74,943k -- a real, quantified improvement. But this operating growth contributed only ~5.4% of the total PBT increase, with the remaining ~94.6% coming from a Net Finance Income swing that is not confirmed to be repeatable, so headline PBT/PAT growth (201-205%) substantially overstates sustainable growth.

valuation.rationale: At Rs.800/share (market cap Rs.5,330.50mn) against total equity of Rs.13,311.30mn (NAV/share ~Rs.1,902 on 7.0mn shares), the stock trades at a substantial ~0.42x discount to book value, and a statistically very cheap ~1.6x annualized P/E -- though the P/E is distorted by unrealised investment gains embedded in the earnings line and should not be read as a clean operating multiple.

business_quality.rationale: By balance-sheet composition (72.0% of total assets in financial investments, >28x the PPE carrying value), RENU is primarily an investment-holding entity that also operates a small city hotel -- an unusual structure. The filing discloses no occupancy rate, ADR, or segmental note for the hotel business, a genuine disclosure gap for assessing hotel-specific business quality.

governance_risk.rationale: A Rs.584,313k residual within Net Finance Income (the dominant driver of this quarter's headline profit growth) is entirely unitemised and unexplained in the filing; combined with a separate FVOCI equity book moving in the opposite direction this quarter (Rs.(45,331)k vs Rs.166,042k gain PY), the investment-portfolio disclosure is genuinely thin for a company where investments dominate the balance sheet.

key_reasons: Substantial discount to net asset value (~0.42x P/B) for a company whose balance sheet is 72.0% financial investments (Rs.9,674.59mn) against a market cap of only Rs.5,330.50mn
The underlying hotel business grew genuinely -- Revenue +45.0% YoY and hotel operating profit +72.0% YoY to Rs.74,943k -- independent of the much larger investment-portfolio swings
Effectively debt-free (only a small Rs.2,344k overdraft, no term borrowings) with a very strong current ratio, providing a defensive balance-sheet floor beneath the discount-to-NAV valuation
watch_factors: 94.6% of this quarter's PBT growth came from Net Finance Income, of which a Rs.584,313k residual (73% of the total Net Finance Income figure) is not itemised anywhere in the filing -- most plausibly unrealised fair-value gains on the investment portfolio, but unconfirmed and inherently reversible

A separate FVOCI equity-investment book moved unfavourably this quarter (Rs.(45,331)k vs a Rs.166,042k gain PY), showing the two investment books can diverge -- the P&L-flattering swing in one does not guarantee the other moves the same way

No occupancy rate, average room rate, or segmental disclosure is given anywhere in the filing -- a genuine gap for assessing the hotel business specifically, and Marketing Expenses (the fastest-growing cost line, +146.1% YoY) warrants monitoring

horizon_notes.6m: Q2 FY2026/27 results will show whether the unexplained Rs.584,313k Net Finance Income residual was a one-off unrealised gain that partially reverses, or reflects a sustained repricing of the investment portfolio.
horizon_notes.1y: If the ~0.42x discount to book narrows even partially while the investment portfolio holds its value and the hotel business keeps growing, there is meaningful re-rating potential; a reversal of unrealised investment gains would be a headwind to headline PAT even if the hotel business keeps improving.
horizon_notes.3y: Thesis depends on management's capital allocation between the hotel operation and the large investment portfolio, and on whether the discount-to-NAV structure persists indefinitely (common for holding-company-like structures on the CSE) or narrows.
horizon_notes.5y: No macro/industry data source in this project to assess Sri Lanka's multi-year tourism cycle (relevant to the small hotel segment) or capital-market conditions relevant to the large investment portfolio that dominates RENU's balance sheet.

interim_updates.note_text: Renuka City Hotels PLC (RENU) reported Profit for the period of Rs.868.68mn for Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026), up 205.1% YoY from Rs.284.79mn a year earlier, on Profit Before Taxation of Rs.870.68mn (+201.5% YoY, 2025: Rs.288.79mn). This headline surge is overwhelmingly a financial-investment-portfolio story, not a hotel-operations one, even though the hotel business itself also grew genuinely: Net Finance Income -- a single combined line on the face P&L covering interest, dividends, and investment gains/losses -- was Rs.795.73mn this quarter versus Rs.245.23mn a year earlier (+224.5% YoY), and this one line alone contributed Rs.550.51mn of the company's total Rs.581.89mn PBT increase, i.e. approximately 94.6% of the ENTIRE profit growth. The hotel business's own Profit From Operations was Rs.74.94mn (2025: Rs.43.56mn), +72.0% YoY -- a real and quantified improvement, but contributing only ~5.4% of the total PBT increase. The Cash Flow Statement's reconciliation shows only Rs.158.97mn Interest Income + Rs.33.99mn Dividend Income + Rs.18.46mn Profit on disposals of shares (Rs.211.42mn combined) of conventional finance income this quarter -- leaving a Rs.584.31mn residual within the Rs.795.73mn Net Finance Income figure that is not itemised anywhere in the filing, most plausibly unrealised fair-value gains on the company's Rs.7,431.56mn 'Investments in financial asset' current-asset holding. Combined with a further Rs.2,243.03mn of non-current investments in financial assets, RENU's total investment portfolio (Rs.9,674.59mn) is 72.0% of Total Assets (Rs.13,439.01mn) and more than 28 times the Rs.333.67mn carrying value of Property, Plant & Equipment -- confirming the company is, by balance sheet composition, primarily an investment-holding entity that also operates a small city hotel. On the hotel side: Revenue grew 45.0% YoY to Rs.63.55mn (2025: Rs.43.82mn), Gross Profit +49.3% to Rs.51.56mn, and Other Operating Income +65.7% to Rs.59.95mn (2025: Rs.36.17mn) -- this Other Operating Income line is now larger than core hotel Gross Profit and is not itemised by source in the filing. Of the operating expense lines, Marketing Expenses grew fastest, +146.1% YoY to Rs.4.80mn (2025: Rs.1.95mn), while Salaries & Related Expenses were the most contained, +4.1% to Rs.11.07mn. Income Tax Expense fell to Rs.2.00mn from Rs.4.00mn PY (-50%) despite the much larger pretax profit, consistent with the profit mix being dominated by lightly-taxed or exempt investment income rather than fully-taxable hotel trading profit -- the filing gives no further breakdown of the tax computation. A separate investment book -- the Fair Value Reserve of equity investments at FVOCI, sitting in Other Comprehensive Income rather than the P&L -- moved UNFAVOURABLY this quarter: Equity Investments at FVTOCI Net Change in Fair Value was Rs.(45.33)mn versus a Rs.166.04mn GAIN a year earlier (-127.3% YoY, a Rs.211.37mn unfavourable swing), which is why Total Comprehensive Income grew a slower 82.6% YoY (Rs.823.34mn vs Rs.450.83mn) even as P&L profit grew a faster 205.1% -- a genuine and quantified divergence between RENU's two separate investment books (the P&L-recognised portfolio driving Net Finance Income, and the OCI-recognised FVOCI equity portfolio).
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: this is the first financial_statements/interim_updates entry for RENU in this database, no prior quarter collected. This filing discloses NO segmental note, NO occupancy rate or average room rate figures, and NO qualitative tourism-season commentary anywhere -- genuine, material disclosure gaps for a hotel operator that were specifically checked for and confirmed absent (unlike some CSE hotel-sector peers, which do disclose occupancy/ADR). The Net Finance Income line (Rs.795,733k this quarter) is presented as a single combined figure with NO split into finance income vs finance cost, and no breakdown of the Rs.584,313k residual not explained by the Interest Income/Dividend Income/Profit-on-disposal add-backs visible in the Cash Flow Statement -- this residual (almost certainly unrealised fair-value gains on the Rs.7,431,559k 'Investments in financial asset' current-asset line) is the single largest driver of this quarter's headline profit growth (~94.6% of the total PBT increase) and cannot be verified or decomposed further from this filing alone; finance_costs is stored as 0 because no finance-cost figure is separately disclosed, not because RENU incurs no finance costs (a genuine mapping gap, not a confirmed zero). The filing does not use a 'Trade Receivables' caption -- trade_receivables is mapped to the closest analogous line, 'Other Receivables' (Rs.4,906k), which may not capture the same scope as a conventional trade-receivables balance for a hotel business (guest/travel-agent debtors); a genuine presentational gap, not resolved by this entry. Other Operating Income (Rs.59,951k this quarter, +65.7% YoY, now larger than hotel Gross Profit) is not broken down by source (e.g. rent, service charges, management fees) anywhere in the filing. The effective tax rate computation (why tax expense FELL YoY despite a much larger pretax profit) is not explained -- plausibly reflects BOI/concessionary tax treatment of investment income, but this is inference, not disclosed fact.
interim_updates.takeaway: RENU's headline 205.1% YoY profit growth is, on close reading of the filing, overwhelmingly an investment-portfolio story rather than a hotel-operations story: Net Finance Income (+224.5% YoY to Rs.795.73mn) contributed roughly 94.6% of the total PBT increase, while the actual hotel business -- though it did grow genuinely, with Profit From Operations up 72.0% YoY to Rs.74.94mn on 45.0% revenue growth -- contributed only about 5.4%. A Rs.584.31mn portion of Net Finance Income is not itemised anywhere in the filing and is most plausibly unrealised fair-value gains on the company's Rs.7,431.56mn financial-asset portfolio, which together with a further Rs.2,243.03mn of non-current investments makes up 72.0% of Total Assets -- by balance-sheet composition RENU is primarily an investment-holding company that happens to operate a small city hotel, not primarily a hotel operator, and this quarter's results should be read with that structure in mind. A separate, OCI-recognised FVOCI equity portfolio moved unfavourably in the opposite direction (Rs.(45.33)mn versus a Rs.166.04mn gain a year earlier), a reminder that RENU carries two distinct investment books whose fortunes can diverge quarter to quarter. On the hotel side itself, Marketing Expenses growing 146.1% YoY is worth watching as the fastest-rising cost line, while no occupancy, ADR, or segmental disclosure is available in this filing to further contextualise the underlying hotel-trading improvement.

Net Finance Income (a single combined P&L line: interest, dividends, investment gains/losses) was Rs.795.73mn, +224.5% YoY (2025: Rs.245.23mn), contributing ~94.6% of the total PBT increase; hotel Profit From Operations was Rs.74.94mn, +72.0% YoY, contributing only ~5.4%.

A Rs.584.31mn residual within Net Finance Income is not itemised in the filing -- almost certainly unrealised fair-value gains on the Rs.7,431.56mn 'Investments in financial asset' current-asset holding, since disclosed Interest Income (Rs.158.97mn) + Dividend Income (Rs.33.99mn) + Profit on disposals of shares (Rs.18.46mn) account for only Rs.211.42mn of the Rs.795.73mn total.
Total investment portfolio (current + non-current 'Investments in financial assets') is Rs.9,674.59mn, 72.0% of Total Assets (Rs.13,439.01mn) and over 28x the Rs.333.67mn PPE carrying value.
Marketing Expenses grew fastest of the opex lines, +146.1% YoY to Rs.4.80mn (2025: Rs.1.95mn); Salaries & Related Expenses grew only +4.1% to Rs.11.07mn, the most contained cost line.

Equity Investments at FVTOCI Net Change in Fair Value (a separate OCI-recognised investment book) swung to Rs.(45.33)mn from a Rs.166.04mn GAIN a year earlier (-127.3% YoY), capping Total Comprehensive Income growth to 82.6% YoY versus 205.1% P&L profit growth.
No segmental note, occupancy rate, average room rate, or tourism-season commentary is disclosed anywhere in this filing.
key_drivers: Net Finance Income (Rs.795.73mn, +224.5% YoY) is the dominant driver of the quarter's profit surge, contributing ~94.6% of the total Rs.581.89mn PBT increase -- predominantly an investment-portfolio effect, not a hotel-operations effect.

An unexplained Rs.584.31mn residual within Net Finance Income (not covered by disclosed interest, dividend, or disposal-gain figures), most plausibly unrealised fair-value gains on the Rs.7,431.56mn FVTPL-type investment portfolio, is the single largest unquantifiable driver behind this quarter's headline profit growth.

Hotel Profit From Operations genuinely grew 72.0% YoY to Rs.74.94mn on 45.0% revenue growth, but this contributed only ~5.4% of the total PBT increase given the much larger scale of Net Finance Income.
Marketing Expenses growing 146.1% YoY (to Rs.4.80mn) is the fastest-growing cost line and the main opex drag on the hotel segment's otherwise strong operating improvement.
